paper: Blattner F. R. et al. (1997) 'The complete genome sequence of Escherichia coli K-12.' Science 277(5331):1453-1462. doi:10.1126/science.277.5331.1453. PMID 9278503.
notes: Five heavy-duty scientifically-open questions surfaced by re-reading extraction/marker.md (which distills the paper's abstract + canonical claims) against modern 2026 knowledge. These are truly open — none are solved by simply re-running annotation. Each has a defensible basis in the paper and a concrete next-steps program.

questions.q: What is the *causal* explanation for the ~55% CDS co-orientation with replication in E. coli, versus the ~75% co-orientation in B. subtilis — and does the residual 45% represent selectively neutral drift, active selection *against* co-orientation for a specific gene class, or a lineage-specific replication-transcription conflict tolerance?
questions.basis: The paper reports that 'guanines, oligonucleotides possibly related to replication and recombination, and most genes' are oriented with the local direction of replication, and gives ~55% for CDS co-orientation. Our reproduction confirms 54.89%. But E. coli's 55% is dramatically weaker than B. subtilis's ~75% (sibling BVBRC-100 Kunst 1997 replication) — despite both being fast-growing Gram-positives-vs-negatives with similar replication-transcription conflict pressure. This 20-percentage-point gap has no accepted mechanistic explanation.
next_steps: Stratify NC_000913.3 CDSs by (a) essentiality (Keio collection), (b) expression rank (RNA-seq compendium, e.g. Ecomics), (c) operon head vs internal, (d) presence in horizontally-transferred islands. Compute co-orientation fraction per stratum.
Repeat for B. subtilis 168 (NC_000964.3) with the same strata; compute stratum-by-stratum ratio.

Test the hypothesis that the E. coli deficit is concentrated in horizontally-transferred / IS-adjacent regions (which would suggest neutral drift on recently-acquired DNA) vs distributed uniformly (which would suggest weakened selection).
If the deficit is HGT-concentrated, quantify the age-since-acquisition dependence using KaKs to the nearest sister lineage.

questions.q: Of the 38% of proteins with 'no attributed function' in 1997, how many remain functionally uncharacterized in 2026 despite 28 years of experimental and computational annotation — and what property predicts persistent unknown-ness?
questions.basis: The abstract states verbatim: 'Of 4288 protein-coding genes annotated, 38 percent have no attributed function.' Modern EcoCyc (2024+) claims that ~90%+ of E. coli K-12 MG1655 proteins have at least some functional annotation, meaning the unknown fraction has dropped from ~1,629 proteins to ~200–400 proteins. The identity, phylogenetic distribution, and structural properties of the *residual* unknown set is the scientifically interesting question — this is the frontier of functional discovery in the best-studied bacterium.
next_steps: Extract the modern EcoCyc 'y-gene' set (proteins with no experimentally verified function) as of 2026 release.
Cross-map to the Blattner 1997 annotation snapshot (recoverable from GenBank U00096.1 history) to identify which 1997-unknowns are still unknown.

Compute predictors of persistent unknown-ness: (a) protein length, (b) transmembrane content (TMHMM/DeepTMHMM), (c) IDR fraction (IUPred/AlphaFold pLDDT), (d) essentiality (Keio), (e) phylogenetic breadth (# orthologs in a pan-bacterial set), (f) AlphaFold structural cluster novelty (Foldseek against PDB + AFDB).
The subset that is (i) still unknown, (ii) essential in Keio, (iii) structurally novel per Foldseek — is a high-value experimental hit list for targeted characterization.

questions.q: Which specific 'patches of unusual composition' identified by Blattner et al. as evidence of horizontal transfer correspond to bona-fide integrative-conjugative elements (ICEs), cryptic prophages, or IS-mediated insertions when re-analyzed with modern mobile-element callers — and what is the resulting revised estimate of *horizontally acquired* genome fraction in MG1655?
questions.basis: The abstract says 'The genome also contains insertion sequence (IS) elements, phage remnants, and many other patches of unusual composition indicating genome plasticity through horizontal transfer.' Our metrics.json reports 50 `mobile_element` annotations in NC_000913.3 but does not classify them. The paper made this observation qualitatively; a quantitative modern re-analysis is a real open contribution.
next_steps: Run ISEScan (IS families), PHASTER-lite (prophages), ICEfinder (ICEs), IslandViewer/AlienHunter (compositional islands) on NC_000913.3.
Cross-reference the 50 GenBank `mobile_element` calls against the union of the four callers; identify concordant vs discordant regions.
Report total bp in each mobile-element class, compute percent-of-genome horizontally-acquired, and compare to Blattner's qualitative estimate.
For each discordant region, produce a mini-vignette (coordinates, GC%, GC-skew signature, nearest orthology in a bacterial reference set) so a human curator can adjudicate.
This produces the first fully-quantified successor to Blattner's qualitative HGT inventory.

questions.q: Does the paper's claimed ABC-transporter paralog family (n=80, 'largest family of paralogous proteins') hold up as the top family under modern clustering — or has an alternative family (e.g. LysR-type transcriptional regulators, MFS transporters, two-component response regulators) overtaken it — and what does the re-ranking say about the paper's implicit model of what drives paralog-family expansion in enteric bacteria?
questions.basis: The abstract asserts 'The largest family of paralogous proteins contains 80 ABC transporters.' Modern EcoCyc lists ~65–75 ABC systems (depending on whether permease-only vs full transporter is counted), and modern LysR-type regulator counts approach ~45 in K-12 alone. The MFS transporter superfamily has grown as InterPro/Pfam definitions widened. Whether ABC transporters are still the top family under a *self-consistent* modern clustering protocol is an open — and paper-testable — question.
next_steps: All-vs-all MMseqs2 clustering of NC_000913.3 proteome at multiple identity/coverage thresholds (30/50/70% id × 50/70/90% coverage) — enumerate top-10 cluster sizes.
Independently: InterPro-domain-based family assignment; enumerate top-10 domain-family sizes.
Independently: Pfam-A + Pfam-B (or ECOD) hierarchical family assignment; enumerate top-10.
Compare all three protocols' top-family rankings against Blattner's ABC claim; report which protocols preserve the ranking vs which invert it.
This addresses a subtle methodological question — was ABC-transporter dominance an artifact of the paper's 1997 clustering protocol, or a robust feature of the genome?

questions.q: Do the 'oligonucleotides possibly related to replication and recombination' whose orientation the paper flagged as replichore-asymmetric (implicitly: KOPS, Chi sites, dnaA-boxes, terminus-utilization sites) show the *same* orientation asymmetry when computed on the modern NC_000913.3 sequence — and are the residual counter-oriented instances concentrated in horizontally-acquired regions (consistent with the HGT-drift hypothesis) or distributed uniformly (consistent with mutational relaxation)?
questions.basis: The abstract couples strand-bias to 'guanines, oligonucleotides possibly related to replication and recombination.' Our reproduction directly tested the CDS strand-bias (54.9%) but did not touch the oligonucleotide-motif orientation, which is the paper's mechanistic hook. Whether the residual counter-oriented KOPS/Chi/dnaA-box instances co-localize with HGT islands (linking Q3 and Q5) is a genuinely-open compositional-genomics question.
next_steps: Enumerate all instances of KOPS (GGGNAGGG), Chi (GCTGGTGG), dnaA-box (TTATCCACA), and terC/dif sites in NC_000913.3 on each strand.
Assign each instance to its replichore; compute co-orientation fraction per motif.
Compare to a null model (dinucleotide-preserving genome shuffle) to test statistical significance of the asymmetry.
For each motif with significant asymmetry, check whether counter-oriented instances are enriched in the mobile-element regions identified in Q3.
Deliverable: a per-motif replichore-orientation table plus a joint HGT-vs-native contingency test — this is exactly the kind of quantitative followup Blattner 1997 telegraphed but did not close.
